title: Asset Management: Hardware, Software, and Data

cards.back: You can only protect, patch, or restore the assets you know about.
Hardware (servers, workstations, mobile), software (OS, applications, libraries), data (databases, files, backups).
Identifier, type, owner, location, version, criticality, data classification, lifecycle state.
Links the asset to its owner, business criticality, processed data, and dependencies.
The owner decides classification and access; the custodian manages the asset day-to-day (storage, backups, patches).
Planning / scoping: define need, criticality, and security requirements before purchase.
Procurement: include encryption, support duration, compliance, and secure erasure in requirements.
Assignment / accounting: assign an owner, register the asset, label, and document authorized use.
Monitoring / asset tracking: patches, movements, usage; detect phantom assets and shadow IT.
Disposal / decommissioning: sanitize or destroy, revoke access and licenses, certify end-of-life.
Network discovery, MDM for mobile devices, CMDB, and periodic reviews.
Asset or service used without the security team's knowledge: it bypasses inventory and controls.
Unpatched, unmonitored, unrestored: a classic entry point and root cause of incidents.
Certificate of destruction or sanitization report: essential to prove end-of-life of media.
Legal retention periods suspend erasure: an asset is not destroyed before the obligation expires.
